title: Denta Water and Infra Solutions Ltd - 544345 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Denta's Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose about 18% but EBITDA declined; management maintains 20% FY27 growth target without quantified financials in the call.
summary.overview: Management described a difficult first half in Karnataka, citing a government transition, monsoon-related disruption to approvals, payments and on-site execution. H1 revenue was cited as about Rs. 128 crore, and Q2 EBITDA fell on high site inventory of uPVC pipes and pumps and projects still in early stages. Order book stood at about Rs. 782 crore (7,824.44 million) as of September 30, 2026, with 32 projects under execution. Management said the FY27 20% revenue growth target is still intended, with clarity promised by end of Q3 or early Q4.

segments.name: Water supply (Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT)
segments.commentary: Three Jal Jeevan Mission projects (Kerehalli, Chikkabenakal, Doddakavalande) are about 75-80% complete; one AMRUT project is active. Management said no work order yet captured under JJM 2.0.

segments.name: Wastewater / sewage treatment
segments.commentary: Sewage treatment plants being set up at ten locations in five Karnataka districts, using CAMUS, NABR and HAP bio-enzyme technologies. Management said Rs. 4,046 million of the order book is water-management related.

segments.name: Irrigation infrastructure
segments.commentary: Two Karnataka Neeravari Nigam orders won in H1 FY27 worth about 655 million, covering jack wells, 5-6 km pumping, and 12-14 check dams. KC Valley: three projects, two completed and one 75-80% complete.

guidance_outlook: Management said it strives to maintain 20% revenue growth for FY27, dependent on Q3 and Q4 revenue; a firm revenue estimate to be communicated by end Q3 or early Q4.
Expects Q3 and Q4 order pipeline/revenue to be about 15-20% higher than H1 FY27.
Expects EBITDA/profit margin moderation due to inflation in petrol and HDPE/PVC raw material costs, but aims for minimum 20% profitability on projects.
Targets completion of most ongoing projects in FY27; KC Valley project expected by end of this year.
Sandur town water supply and reuse project (about Rs. 850 crore, DBOT model, 2-3 year timeline) tender expected in H2 FY27, timing not confirmed.
capex_capacity: Standalone execution capacity cited up to Rs. 300 crore per single project; about 30 ongoing projects valued around 7,824 million.
Plans for sewage treatment plants at ten locations in five Karnataka districts; project cost for technology partners around 20-25% of project cost, with 5-year monitoring contracts.
Post-award timeline for DBOT projects: design 3-6 months, procurement 3-6 months, execution starting 8-9 months after award.
Company described as virtually debt-free with minimal financing costs; no capex figure disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q2 EBITDA decline attributed to high site inventory of uPVC pipes, pumps and similar materials on projects at early implementation stages, with milestone billing not yet reached.
Monsoon in Karnataka (June to September/October) and government transition delayed approvals, payments and road execution; 224 of 246 Karnataka taluks declared drought-hit per management.
Pipeline diversification: tenders in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu were floated but postponed; bids being evaluated for profitability.
Management said it aims for minimum 20% profit on projects, with input cost variation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 on receivables and order conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing JJM 1 projects are 75-80% complete with funds allocated by state; no JJM 2.0 work order captured yet, so no timing on payments can be given.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 20% revenue growth guidance be maintained given H1 revenue of about Rs. 128 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it strives to maintain 20% growth, dependent on Q3 and Q4; will update by end of Q3 on likely FY27 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables position and plans to manage working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables were 164.60 million at Sept 30, 2026; about 107.6 million collected by October 31, leaving 57.62 million outstanding.

qa_highlights.question: Reducing dependence on Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects identified in Odisha, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; one or two tenders postponed; bids will be made only if viable and margins are good.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build-up of uPVC pipes and pumps at early-stage sites ahead of milestone billing; some collections slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company execute a large project like Sandur without straining the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is virtually debt-free and can fund large DBOT projects from internal resources; execution begins 8-9 months post award.

risks_watch: Q2 EBITDA decline and margin moderation from raw material inflation (HDPE, PVC, petrol costs).
Receivables from government and PSU clients (164.60 million at Sept 30) and delayed payments; JJM 2.0 order capture not yet achieved.
Geographic concentration in Karnataka; out-of-state tenders postponed.
H1 revenue run-rate of about Rs. 128 crore requires sharp H2 ramp-up to reach 20% FY27 growth target.
Reliance on government budgets (JJM, AMRUT, state schemes) and a pending large Sandur tender (about Rs. 850 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term prospects and order visibility, but cautious and often vague on near-term numbers: revenue, EBITDA and tender timing were given as ranges or deferred to end-Q3. Management repeatedly attributed delays to the Karnataka government transition and monsoon conditions.
key_quotes: We hope to and we strive to maintain 20% growth for the year Financial Year '26-27.
As far as Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 is concerned, we have not yet captured any work order under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.
Virtually, not much debt is being incurred by the company, thus reducing the financial costs.
If we get good favorable economical order and if it is workable, then only we will back those orders.
